theorems.name: K4 chirality gauge classification
theorems.statement: The six F2 handoff bits modulo four vertex sign gauges are completely classified by three independent triangle holonomies; C1(K4;F2)/delta C0(K4;F2) is F2^3.

theorems.name: Global signed-generator criterion
theorems.statement: A global signed J exists iff all three independent triangle holonomies vanish.

theorems.name: Global chirality is a two-element torsor
theorems.statement: Every trivial handoff system has exactly two trivializations, differing by simultaneous reversal of all four local generators; nontrivial classes have none.

theorems.name: No canonical full-S4 chirality choice
theorems.statement: The two tetrahedral orientations form the sign torsor: A4 preserves each choice and every odd permutation exchanges them, so unoriented K4 incidence cannot select one S4-invariant signed generator.

theorems.name: O(2) semidirect globalization
theorems.statement: Before a global chirality choice, finite phase transport has structure C_N semidirect C2, with the nontrivial C2 element acting by inversion; after completion this is U(1) semidirect C2 isomorphic to O(2).

theorems.name: Involutive phases survive chirality reversal
theorems.statement: In any commutative phase group, every element h with h^2=1 is fixed by the inversion handoff and is central in the associated G semidirect C2 rotation/reflection group.

theorems.name: Orientation-independent Euler half-turn
theorems.statement: The complex phase -1 is fixed by every chirality handoff and central in the O(2) globalization; therefore exp(J_v*pi_rot)=-1 descends across all four slices even when the signed generators J_v do not glue.

theorems.name: Maximal orientation-forgetting finite phase set
theorems.statement: For every even C_N, inversion fixes exactly 0 and N/2; hence identity and half-turn are the only phases that descend through arbitrary chirality reversals.
